title: Resume-to-interview traceability and avoiding unverifiable claims
objectives: Trace every Salesforce resume bullet to a story, artifact, or credential page you can defend in the interview.
Avoid unverifiable claims: invented metrics, other people's Apex, unearned certifications, dump-based 'exam expertise.'
Align resume wording with Trailhead accuracy: action verbs, dates, no lying, match the posting with skills you have.
Fix inflated bullets before the interview rather than hoping they will not be probed.
diagnostic_question: Your resume says 'Led Salesforce CLM and saved 40%.' You configured a validation rule. What is unverifiable, and how do you rewrite the bullet so interview traceability holds?
definition: Resume-to-interview traceability means every claim on the resume can be walked to evidence in the room: a project slice, a STAR story, a Trailhead credential, or a labeled playground. Avoiding unverifiable claims means you do not invent metrics, titles, or certs. Trailhead resume and career modules require accuracy, dates, action verbs, and demonstrable skills—do not lie. ([Resume Writing Strategies](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/resume-strategies); [Plan your resume](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/resume-strategies/resume-plan); [Land your next opportunity](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/career-development-planning/land-your-next-opportunity))
why_it_matters: Interviewers pick the strongest verb on the page and ask for a deep-dive. Unverifiable claims collapse under CAREER-007 questions. Inflated certs are an integrity failure against official credential pages.
sixty_second_explanation: Treat the resume like a chain of custody for exhibits. Every bullet is an evidence bag with a tag that must still match in the interview room. If the tag says you led CLM and the bag only contains a validation rule, the chain is broken. Unverifiable claims are bags with no exhibit—or someone else's exhibit with your name on the tag.
deeper_explanation: Plan Your Resume lists four must-haves: contact, education, skills/mastery, work/volunteer experience. It tells you to use the job description's skills you actually have. ([Plan your resume](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/resume-strategies/resume-plan))

Land-your-next-opportunity: action verbs, accomplishments with results, be accurate, include dates, do not lie. Job titles should not lie. ([Land your next opportunity](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/career-development-planning/land-your-next-opportunity))

Official credential pages exist so you can claim Platform Administrator, Platform Developer, App Builder, Business Analyst, or Application Architect only if earned. ([Platform Administrator](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/platformadministrator); [Platform Developer](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/platformdeveloperi/); [Business Analyst](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/businessanalyst))

Get Job Ready and Interview Strategies are the practice path that makes traceability real: resume plus rehearsed stories. ([Get Job Ready](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/get-job-ready); [Interview Strategies](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/interview-strategies))
Trailhead ranks and badges are skills evidence; they are not secret job titles and not certifications.

mental_model.analogy: Chain of custody for evidence bags: every resume bullet is a tagged exhibit that must still match in the interview room.
useful_mapping: teammate's Apex with your name → tampered tag
playground labeled as playground → honest bag
dump expertise → contraband, not an exhibit
where_it_breaks: Resumes are short; not every exhibit fits on the page—still, nothing on the page may be fake.
This is not a crime-lab product.
Recruiters may have rewritten your bullet; you still must correct it before the interview.
Badges are not chain-of-custody for production outcomes.

teach_back_prompt: Take three resume bullets. For each, name the interview exhibit or rewrite the bullet until the chain of custody holds.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Every resume bullet must open an exhibit: story, artifact, or earned credential. I rewrite unverifiable metrics, stolen Apex, and fake certs before the interview.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I audit bullets against Trailhead accuracy. Led versus configured. Percents need sources. Certs must match official pages I hold. Dumps are not expertise. Playground work is labeled. If a recruiter inflated a line, I correct it in the room and on the page. Traceability is chain of custody, not clever wording.

terminology.plain: A path from bullet to exhibit.
terminology.precise: Resume line → STAR/deep-dive/credential/playground label that survives a probe.
terminology.example: Configured Opportunity legal freeze; exhibit = validation rule + UAT notes.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Requirements traceability: a BA term; cousin idea, different artifact.
terminology.boundary: If you cannot open the bag in 60 seconds, rewrite.

terminology.plain: A statement the interviewer cannot audit.
terminology.precise: Invented ROI, others' code, unearned certs, dump mastery, fake titles.
terminology.non_example: Reversals 6→0 per a named report you built.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Ambiguous claim: unclear but fixable with a rewrite.
terminology.boundary: Silence is better than a fake percent.

terminology.plain: A certification listed on an official Trailhead credential page that you hold.
terminology.precise: Platform Administrator, Platform Developer, Business Analyst, etc.—only if true.
terminology.example: Linking to the credential page you passed.
terminology.non_example: Admin certified because you finished a trailmix.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Badge/superbadge: skills evidence, not the same as a certification.
terminology.boundary: Names change; copy the live page.

terminology.plain: A verb or scope larger than your pack.
terminology.example: Led CLM → Configured Closed Won freeze and UAT.
terminology.boundary: Recruiters inflate; you still own the words.

terminology.plain: Expertise based on unofficial exam items.
terminology.precise: Forbidden by handbook source policy and Salesforce exam integrity.
terminology.non_example: Studied official cert-prep Trailhead and Help.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Cert-prep module: official study, not a dump.

terminology.plain: Resume must-have for skills you can show.
terminology.precise: Plan Your Resume: skills and mastery as one of four must-haves, aligned to the posting.
terminology.example: Flow, sharing, Apex tests—each with a story.
terminology.non_example: Listing every Salesforce cloud including ones you never opened.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Keywords: match posting language only for skills you have.
terminology.boundary: ATS keywords do not justify lying.

terminology.precise: Trailhead Playground / DE / volunteer, named as such.
terminology.example: Built LAB_ freeze in a playground (not a bank).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Volunteer nonprofit org: real job-like if true.

terminology.precise: Integrity move when the page still lies; then update the file.
terminology.example: The bullet says led; I configured the freeze—here is the slice.
terminology.non_example: Defending the lie because the recruiter wrote it.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Errata: a written follow-up with a corrected resume.
terminology.boundary: Do not wait for them to catch you.

when_to_use: When you must enforce resume-to-interview traceability before a Salesforce loop.
When a bullet contains an unverifiable metric, title, or certification.
When a recruiter rewrote your verbs larger than your pack.
When you need to label playground work honestly.
When dump language or unearned credentials appear on the page.
when_not_to_use: Do not keep an inflated bullet because it 'gets interviews' if you cannot defend it.
Do not claim a Trailhead badge as a Salesforce certification.
Do not treat ATS keyword stuffing as permission to list unearned clouds.
Do not use unofficial exam dumps as resume proof.
Do not paste customer confidential metrics onto a public resume.
configuration_or_code_location: Trailhead credentials page for certs you hold
Not Setup, not production reports with PII on a public PDF

worked_example.scenario: Resume-to-interview traceability audit: three bullets (1) Led Salesforce CLM and saved 40% (2) Platform Developer certified (you are not) (3) Built LAB_ freeze in a playground listed as 'Bank of Example production lead.' You must avoid unverifiable claims.
inputs: True work: validation rule + UAT; unknown savings

decisions.decision: Rehearse a STAR for the rewritten freeze bullet.
decisions.because: Traceability is not only a rewrite; it is a probe rehearsal.

New (3): Designed a legal-freeze prototype in a Trailhead Playground (synthetic data).

hands_on_lab.environment: Your resume draft. No production customer data on a public copy.
starting_state_checks: You know which certs you actually hold
steps: List every Salesforce bullet and cert line.
For each, write the exhibit (story, URL, playground) or FLAG.
Open official credential pages for any cert named; delete mismatches.
Rewrite FLAG lines with accurate verbs.
Run a 60-second probe on each remaining bullet with a peer or timer.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Take a job posting and highlight only skills you can trace; do not add clouds you have not used.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Remove PII and client names if required
hands_on_lab.limitations: Recruiter portals may still show an old file—upload the corrected one.

interview_questions.question: What is resume-to-interview traceability?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Every bullet is an evidence bag I can open with a story, artifact, or earned credential. Unverifiable claims get rewritten before the loop.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I audit verbs, percents, and certs against Trailhead accuracy and official credential pages. I label playgrounds. I rehearse probes. I would rather a smaller true page than a large empty one. Dumps are not exhibits.
interview_questions.example: Configured freeze bullet opens a STAR; fake 40% is removed.
follow_ups: What if you have little experience?

interview_questions.question: How do you avoid unverifiable claims on a Salesforce resume?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No unsourced percents, no unearned certs, no stolen Apex, no dump flex, no unlabeled playgrounds.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use action verbs tied to my pack. I copy credential names only from pages I passed. I match posting keywords only for skills I can demonstrate. I correct recruiter inflation. Get Job Ready is the practice path that makes this survive speech.
interview_questions.example: Delete PD until passed; list Admin if passed; playground labeled.

interview_questions.question: Rewrite 'Led Salesforce CLM and saved 40%.'
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Configured Opportunity Closed Won legal freeze and UAT; savings unknown / not measured.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I drop led and 40%. I name the object and my pack. If I have reversals from a report, I may cite that instead of 40%. I prepare the STAR. I do not keep CLM lead unless I owned that program.
interview_questions.example: Optional true add: reversals 6→0 per ops report if sourced.
tradeoffs: How much detail on a resume
follow_ups: What if ops wants the 40% line?

interview_questions.question: You are not PD certified; the posting requires it. What goes on the resume?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Do not list the credential. You may list official prep and related true skills; do not fake the seal.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the Platform Developer page and I do not borrow it. I can say I am scheduled or studying via official cert-prep if true. I still need traceable Apex/LWC bullets if I claim those skills. Lying to pass ATS fails the interview and is an integrity issue.
interview_questions.example: Skills: Apex tests in a playground (labeled). Certs: Platform Administrator only if held.

interview_questions.question: They probe a bullet you cannot defend. Recover.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Correct immediately, give the true slice, and offer an updated resume.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not blame-shift without a fix. I say the line is inflated, here is what I actually did, here is the exhibit. I follow Interview Strategies follow-up with a clean PDF. CAREER-007 deep-dive continues on the true work.
interview_questions.example: Architected → I configured the freeze; developer Maya owned the callout.

interview_questions.question: Every bullet flagged in your audit. You still need a resume.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Write smaller true lines from playground, volunteer, or coursework—and label them.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Plan Your Resume still wants experience, even volunteer. A labeled DE project with a STAR is an exhibit. Empty bags are worse than a short honest page. Get Job Ready exists for this stage. Do not invent a bank.
interview_questions.example: Volunteer: helped a nonprofit admin with reports (named tasks). Playground: LAB_ freeze.

interview_questions.question: How do you design a bullet-to-exhibit table?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Columns: bullet, verb pack, metric source, cert URL, STAR id, flag. Flags must be rewritten before sending.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I go line by line. Cert column only holds official pages I passed. Metric column holds report names or unknown. STAR id links CAREER-008. I run 60-second probes. I store the table privately, not on the public PDF.
interview_questions.example: Row: Configured freeze | I | reversals report | n/a | STAR-conflict | OK.
follow_ups: Share the table with a mentor?

interview_questions.question: Teach chain-of-custody for resumes and where the analogy breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Tagged bags must match the room. It breaks because resumes are short and this is not a crime lab—but empty bags still fail.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Bullets are tags, stories are openings, credential pages are seals, fake percents are empty, stolen Apex is tampering, dumps are contraband. It breaks when recruiters retag without you—you still recustodiate. I then rewrite the CLM 40% line live.
interview_questions.example: Configured freeze; unknown savings; no PD seal.
